title: Selecting Spanish translates only the nav rail and Settings; every other screen stays English
summary: The inherited verdict is stale in one half and still true in the other, so I fixed the half that has a removable cause. STALE: an earlier wave already made the picker honest (the option is labelled '(beta)', the subtitle is scoped) — general_settings.dart:75-105, pinned by general_language_scope_test.dart. STILL TRUE AND FIXED HERE: the setting's own scoped claim — 'the language used for app CHROME' — was itself false. The persistent status bar IS chrome (it is the one strip on every screen) and it was 100% hard-coded English: 'Camera Disconnected', 'Mount Disconnected', 'Guider Disconnected', 'Focus', 'Idle', 'No save path', 'Dashboard' — the exact strings the audit read off the Spanish build. status_bar.dart, its four part files and the title bar's two icon tooltips now render through l10n, reusing the catalogue's existing short-word vocabulary (mount/focus/guiding/disconnected/idle/sequenceRunning/sequencePaused/dashboardTitle) and adding 30 keys in both locales. SequenceStatusVisuals.of (sequence_status_visuals.dart:28) — the shared (colour, label, icon) tuple behind the status LED, the sequencer toolbar badge, the mobile playback bar and the mini bar — now takes a REQUIRED SkotiqLocalizations rather than returning English literals; required and not optional-with-a-default, because a silent English fallback there is exactly how the bar stayed English while the chrome around it translated. Separately the Spanish subtitle was hard-coded in the widget with a ternary while the catalogue key generalLanguageDesc still held the original false claim 'Elegir el idioma de la interfaz principal'; the honest sentence now lives in the catalogue and the ternary is gone, so every reader of that key gets the truth. NOT FIXED, stated plainly: the product screens (Dashboard body, Imaging, Sequencer, Analytics) are still English — 50 of the app's 847 files call l10n. I checked the cheap hypothesis first (that the catalogue was merely unwired): 192 of its 498 keys have no caller, but reading them one by one shows navScience/navFraming/navPlanetarium/navYourSky/navConstellation/navTransients are orphaned because those destinations were FOLDED into other screens (shell_navigation.dart:49-55), and most planner/analytics orphans are leftovers from screen rewrites. The residue is a translation program, not a wiring bug.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/status_bar_localization_test.dart -> 'the status bar follows the chosen language' (pumps the real StatusBar under Locale('es') and asserts Cámara / Montura / Guía / Enfoque / Desconectado / Inactivo / 'Sin ruta de guardado' / Panel render, and that Camera / Mount / Disconnected / 'No save path' / Idle / Dashboard do NOT) and 'an English build is untouched'. pumpAppScreen gained an opt-in `locale` so a tree can be read in the locale the setting stores; general_language_scope_test now uses it instead of relying on the deleted ternary.
revert_check: Replaced `label: l10n.text('statusCamera'),` with `label: 'Camera',` in status_bar.dart (the Camera pill). 'the status bar follows the chosen language' FAILED — 'Found 0 widgets with text "Cámara"'; 'an English build is untouched' still passed. Restored -> 2/2 pass.
caveats: The scope boundary is the app's own word, 'chrome': status bar, nav rail, title bar, Settings. Two widgets HOSTED in the bar are still English and are shared with other screens — EquipmentStatusIndicator (chip reads '3/5' or 'N connected'; its popup menu is English) and OperationStatusBar. Neither appears in the finding's evidence, because the audit profile had no active equipment profile so the chip never rendered. Dashboard body, Imaging, Sequencer and Analytics remain English.

title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them
summary: Closed by wave 4 at BOTH levels the verifier's correction named, and the correction was the important half. (a) The picker no longer offers IANA names it cannot honour: location_settings.dart:452 feeds `kUtcOffsetTimezones` (:867) and `migrateLegacyTimezone` maps a stored IANA label through `kLegacyIanaUtcOffsets` (:911, :843-855), so an existing 'Asia/Tokyo' resolves to an offset the parser accepts. (b) The surfaces now CONSULT the clock instead of formatting DateTime.now(): status bar at status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart:147 `ref.watch(clockProvider).fromUtc(now.toUtc())`, dashboard header at dashboard_header_actions.dart:102, night-timeline axis + countdown at night_timeline.dart:41, moon rise/set at moon_card.dart:37. The verifier's point was that widening the parser alone would have left the bar exactly as broken; that is not what shipped. location_settings.dart:816-830 also derives the row's own subtitle from clockProvider, so the row cannot claim an offset the app is not running on.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/status_bar_timezone_test.dart -> 'the status-bar clock follows the chosen site timezone', '"Use system time" leaves the status-bar clock host-local', 'the dashboard header clock follows the chosen site timezone'; test/screens/settings/location_settings_truth_test.dart -> 'Timezone every offered value actually drives the clock', 'a stored IANA label is migrated so the choice takes effect', 'the row reports the clock the app is really running on'. All green.
revert_check: Independently re-run this wave: replaced `final displayNow = ref.watch(clockProvider).fromUtc(now.toUtc());` with `final displayNow = now;` in status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart. 'the status-bar clock follows the chosen site timezone' FAILED (offset 0 instead of 18000 s); the system-time case still passed. Restored -> green.
caveats: FixedOffsetClock is a fixed offset with no DST rule — the Timezone row's own subtitle says so. Timestamps outside the dashboard/shell (FITS headers, log lines) stay host-local.

title: 'Use Device Location' is IP geolocation labelled as GPS, and it leaves the old elevation in place
summary: Closed by an earlier wave on all three points. The row is titled 'Detect Location' with the subtitle 'Device GPS if this machine has it, otherwise a city-level estimate from your IP address' (location_settings.dart:258-262); a consent dialog naming ipapi.co and its ip-api.com fallback and the ~10 km accuracy is shown BEFORE any request leaves the machine (:513-568); and the elevation is no longer inherited blindly — a fix more than 25 km from the stored site clears it to the app's own 0 m 'not set' value and the snackbar says so (:487, :580-594 `elevation: keepElevation ? settings.elevation : 0`).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/location_settings_truth_test.dart -> 'Detect Location is not labelled GPS', 'asks before anything leaves the machine', 'a fix at another site clears the inherited elevation', 'a fix at the same site keeps the elevation'. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: replaced `elevation: keepElevation ? settings.elevation : 0,` with `elevation: settings.elevation,`. 'a fix at another site clears the inherited elevation' FAILED (expected 0, actual 1234.0). Restored -> green.

title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima
summary: Closed by wave 3, and it matches the verifier's own analysis that the shippable defect is the silence rather than the numbers (the 8-sector model is the app's horizon model everywhere and the reduction is conservative). The import now counts the samples and shows a confirmation before storing anything: location_settings.dart:704-724 states the sample count, that Skotiq keeps eight 45° sectors with only the tallest sample per sector, 'At most 8 of the N survive', and the CONSEQUENCE in the operator's terms — 'part of a sector that is really clear will be treated as blocked and the planner will skip targets there'. It then lists the eight values it is about to store, and Cancel leaves the existing mask untouched. The Local Horizon Mask section states the 8-sector resolution where the values are edited (:327-331).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/location_horizon_import_disclosure_test.dart -> 'the import states the sample count and what it drops', 'shows the eight values it is about to store', 'cancelling leaves the existing mask untouched', 'accepting stores the sectors and the message reports the reduction', 'a single-sample file is not reported as dropping samples'. Green, plus location_horizon_import_authority_test.dart.
revert_check: Independently re-run: deleted the reduction sentence from the confirmation (location_settings.dart:719-721) leaving only 'imported.'. 'the import states the sample count and what it drops' FAILED ('Found 0 widgets with text containing At most 8 of the 36'). Restored -> 5/5 pass.
caveats: The stored model is still eight sectors; a full interpolated profile remains a feature, not a defect fix.

title: Settings search is a raw substring match, so 'capture folder' returns 'No settings match your search'
summary: Closed by an earlier wave exactly where the verifier's correction pointed. settings_screen.dart:172-179 splits the query on whitespace and requires EVERY token to match (`tokens.every((token) => sectionMatchesToken(section, token))`); sectionMatchesToken (:44-47) consults kSettingsSearchSynonyms (:30), which carries the app's own vocabulary for this feature — 'capture folder', 'capture directory', 'save path', 'image folder', 'disk space', 'free space', 'storage location' — for files-storage. SettingsSectionDef.matches (settings_catalog.dart:79-88) survives as the per-token predicate, which is correct: tokenisation belongs to the caller.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/settings_search_query_test.dart -> 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting', 'every token still has to match something', 'an autofocus term does not land on Files & Storage', 'the best match is listed first', + index-hygiene cases. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: replaced the token loop with `if (section.matches(query))` (the pre-fix behaviour). 'a two-word phrase finds the page that owns the setting' FAILED — the screen rendered 'No settings match your search.' for 'capture folder', the finding's exact repro. Restored -> 6/6 pass.

title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Backup & Restore says a real timestamp
summary: Closed, and my revert-check found it is closed TWICE over, which is worth recording because a single-line revert does not expose it. auto_save_settings.dart:169 watches autoSaveLifecycleProvider — the only provider that loads the persisted `autosave.*` keys and calls start(config, lastBackup) — instead of the raw autoSaveServiceProvider, whose instance is rebuilt on every backend swap with compiled-in defaults and a status that says the machine has never been backed up. Independently, :193 reads `ref.watch(autoSaveStatusProvider).valueOrNull ?? service.status`, and autoSaveStatusProvider backfills lastBackup from the persisted `autosave.last_backup_at` — the same key Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore reads. Either path alone renders the truth, so the two surfaces can no longer disagree, and the 'stronger repro' (relaunch on the same profile) is covered because both paths read persisted state rather than session state.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart -> 'Status shows the persisted last backup, not "Never"' (seeds autosave.last_backup_at 2 h old, asserts '2h ago' and that neither 'Never' nor 'Pending' renders), plus the schedule-hydration and no-clobber cases. Green.
revert_check: Reverting EITHER path alone leaves the test passing — I checked both: with the page pointed back at the raw service the 'Never' case still passed (autoSaveStatusProvider backfilled), and with `final status = service.status;` it also still passed (the lifecycle provider had hydrated the instance). Reverting BOTH together FAILED it: 'Found 0 widgets with text "2h ago"'. Restored both -> 3/3 pass. Recording this because wave 4's revert-check named only the lifecycle line, which on its own does not sever this claim.

title: Automatic backups are ON by default and write to a location the Files & Storage page never names and offers no way to change
summary: Both reproduced halves are closed. PATH: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 `_getBackupDirectory` calls resolveDefaultBackupDirectory (:130-139), which resolves 'backups/' beside the resolved database file and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR — the verifier confirmed this live (the sandboxed instance wrote into its own data dir and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups received nothing). DISCLOSURE: wave 3 added a 'Backups' row (file_path_settings.dart:288-291) carrying the real path, asked of `backupServiceProvider.getBackupDirectory()` via backupDirectoryPathProvider (:54) so it cannot drift, plus the unconditional sentence that 'Maximum backups' deletes the oldest bundles from that folder (:277-280) and an Open-folder / Copy-path action. The verifier read the Status section of Automatic Backups and concluded the page never names the folder; Settings > Files & Storage is FilesAndStorageSettings (merged_sections.dart:92-107), which renders FilePathSettings and AutoSaveSettings on ONE page, so that row is on the same scroll.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/file_path_backup_folder_test.dart -> 'the backup folder is named on the page', 'the row says retention deletes from that folder', 'the folder can be opened from the row', 'an unresolvable folder still states the retention policy'. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: renamed the row title from 'Backups' to 'Backups (severed)'. 'the backup folder is named on the page' FAILED ('Found 0 widgets with text "Backups"'). Restored -> 4/4 pass.
caveats: Deliberately NOT built, same call wave 4 made: a user-SELECTABLE backup folder. That needs a new persisted setting plus BackupService write/list/restore plumbing — a feature — and neither reproduced defect (undisclosed path, ignoring the configured data dir) survives without it.

title: The Alpaca server address can never be set
summary: Closed after the verifier's pass. connection_settings.dart:201-217 renders an 'Alpaca Server Address' row whose subtitle is the live `${settings.alpacaServerHost}:${settings.alpacaServerPort}` and whose Configure button opens AlpacaServerDialog (connection_settings_alpaca_dialog.dart), which validates the port and writes through setAlpacaServerHost / setAlpacaServerPort — the skotiq_core setters the finding showed had zero UI callers anywhere. It sits directly above the 'Query Alpaca on startup' toggle (:218-226) whose subtitle refers to 'the configured Alpaca server', so that phrase now has a referent. The verifier's grep was run against a tree that predates this row (connection_settings.dart was last written at 23:33 on 2026-08-03; the aggregated findings file is timestamped 01:22).
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_alpaca_address_test.dart -> 'the Alpaca address is shown and can be changed' (asserts the stored alpacaServerHost becomes 192.168.1.47 and alpacaServerPort 32323, and that the row's subtitle re-renders them), 'a malformed port is refused rather than coerced'. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: corrupted the row title to 'Alpaca Server Addr3ss'. Both cases FAILED ('Found 0 widgets with text "Alpaca Server Address"'), i.e. the tests depend on the row existing and on its write-through, not on a stub. Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently
summary: Closed exactly where the verifier said the decision lives. The connect dialog records whether it is displacing a local FfiBackend (connection_settings.dart:558-560 `hadLocalBackend`) and, when the handshake fails, calls _restoreLocalBackend() -> backendProvider.notifier.useLocalBackend() (:586-587, :605-607) before reporting 'Connection failed: <e>\nStill working locally on this computer.'; a restore that itself fails is named rather than hidden (:592-598). Separately the Connection page renders a 'Work Locally' row whenever the backend is disconnected on a desktop platform (:143-158) — the missing UI caller for useLocalBackend() the verifier flagged, which was why relaunching was the only way back. The red shell banner is unchanged and still keyed on `sequencerBackendProvider is DisconnectedBackend`; it simply no longer fires, because a failed optional connect no longer installs one.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_settings_local_fallback_test.dart -> 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode', 'a disconnected desktop is offered a way back to local mode'. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: replaced `final restoreError = hadLocalBackend ? await _restoreLocalBackend() : null;` with `final String? restoreError = null;`. 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode' FAILED (useLocalBackend called 0 times, expected 1); the 'way back' case still passed. Restored -> 2/2 pass.

title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database, so the app offers to resume a sequence its own database has never heard of — and the failure dialog contradicts itself
summary: Both halves are closed. CROSS-DATABASE (the half the verifier escalated after it STARTED a run against a tree the database had never seen): app_shell.dart:114 resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory anchors the checkpoint on the open database's folder plus a checkpoints/ subdir, and :138 adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint migrates the old application-support file only when SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR is unset; the production call site is :621-626, so getApplicationSupportDirectory is no longer the checkpoint home. SELF-CONTRADICTION: runAppCheckpointRecovery now takes a `checkpointStillResumable` probe (production wiring at :659, backend.getCheckpointInfo()?.canResume), re-reads it after every failed attempt and passes a CheckpointAttemptFailure (:61-67) to the dialog; :189-193 states what is true NOW ('This checkpoint can no longer be resumed. Discard it to clear the prompt.') instead of the unconditional 'still available', drops the Retry action when the checkpoint is gone, and :258 renders the error through describeCheckpointFailure() (:76) so a raw 'Exception: …' never reaches the operator. A probe that itself throws is read as not-resumable.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/shell/checkpoint_recovery_dialog_test.dart -> 'a checkpoint that cannot be resumed is not called available', 'the failure reads as a sentence, not as a Dart object', 'a failed attempt re-reads whether the checkpoint survived', 'a probe that itself fails reports the checkpoint as unusable'; test/screens/shell/checkpoint_directory_test.dart covers the anchoring + legacy adoption. Green.
revert_check: Independently re-run: forced `canRetry = true` with the old unconditional sentence and put `'${failure.error}'` back in place of describeCheckpointFailure(...). 'a checkpoint that cannot be resumed is not called available' and 'the failure reads as a sentence, not as a Dart object' both FAILED (the second found a widget containing 'Exception:'). Restored -> 9/9 pass.
caveats: The dialog's frame count still comes from the checkpoint file rather than from a database query. With the checkpoint now anchored beside the open database that is the same run's own record, so it is no longer a cross-database claim — but it is a file read, not a `SELECT`.
